source_document.body:
Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories (SEL) is investing more than $500 million to expand U.S. manufacturing , with projects in Idaho, Washington, Indiana, and North Carolina scheduled between 2026 and 2028.
What’s Related
The company makes electronic devices that protect, monitor, and control electric power systems. In its Oct. 8 announcement , SEL said demand is growing as customers invest in electric utilities, grid upgrades, data centers, and industrial infrastructure . The plan includes new factories, conversions of existing buildings, and expanded assembly operations.
Several projects were announced earlier, including facilities in Nampa and Post Falls, Idaho, and the purchase of a former building supply property in Pullman, Washington.
Where SEL is expanding
SEL outlined six facility projects, with operations or completion expected in 2027:
Moscow, Idaho : More than $70 million for a new, 305,000-square-foot electronic device factory, expected to be operational by the end of 2027.
Nampa, Idaho : A $150 million investment in property, equipment, and people to convert a 103,000-square-foot building into an electronic device factory. Operations are expected to begin in early 2027, with 250 employees initially.
Post Falls, Idaho: A $150 million investment in property, equipment and people to convert a commercial building into an electronics factory. Operations are expected to begin in late 2027, with 250 employees initially.
Pullman, Washington : Conversion of a 135,810-square-foot building on an 11.5-acre property into a manufacturing operation. The facility is expected to open in early 2027 and employ about 300 people.
West Lafayette, Indiana: A $25 million expansion of board assembly operations, expected to increase production by more than 35%.
Charlotte, North Carolina: A $15 million expansion adding more than 50,000 square feet of custom panel assembly space.
The earlier Nampa announcement said the factory will make electronic devices similar to those produced at SEL’s existing factories in Pullman and Lewiston, Idaho. SEL President Dave Whitehead said the expansion would help reduce lead times and increase production.
According to the company, the approximately 300 employees will include existing SEL employees and new hires. The building previously housed a hardware store, warehouse , and lumberyard.
More equipment, shifts, and manufacturing workers
SEL is also investing more than $100 million in manufacturing equipment. Along with more than 600 additional assemblers and new shifts in Pullman and Lewiston, the company expects electronic device output to rise by an estimated 40% to 60%.
The employee-owned company has also raised manufacturing starting wages to attract and retain workers. In its August wage announcement , SEL set starting pay at $26 an hour for day shifts, $31 for swing shifts, and $36 for night and weekend shifts, effective Aug. 16.
Those increases followed an April adjustment that raised the manufacturing starting wage to $21.50 an hour. SEL said the additional pay is intended to help it hire and retain the workers needed to meet customer demand.
